# Best Portable Power Stations for Camping

For most weekend campers, a **250–500Wh LiFePO4 unit** is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry, and it covers phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP for several nights. If you run a fridge or electric cooler, you'll need a bigger unit.

## Top picks by need

**Best overall for weekend camping: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**
- 288Wh, 300W AC, about 8.3 lb, around $249
- Reviewers call it the easiest of the group to pack. Jackery's US site no longer lists it, though it's still sold through Amazon and other retailers. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty.
- Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Jackery Explorer 300 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+300+Plus)

**Best value: EcoFlow River 3 Plus**
- 286Wh, 600W AC, about 9.9 lb, around $269–299
- It roughly doubles the Jackery's AC output and can expand to 572Wh with an add-on battery.
- Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- Buy: [Amazon search for EcoFlow River 3 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EcoFlow+River+3+Plus)

**Best budget: Bluetti EB3A**
- 268Wh, 600W AC, about 10.1 lb, around $179 (often lower on sale)
- Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Bluetti EB3A](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bluetti+EB3A)

**Best for longer trips: Anker SOLIX C300**
- 288Wh, 300W AC (600W surge), about 9.3 lb, around $199
- It has a built-in retractable lantern and Anker's 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the AC-outlet C300, not the AC-less DC variant.
- Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Anker SOLIX C300](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C300)

**Best for car camping with a fridge: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**
- 890Wh measured, 1,800W AC, 25.2 lb, on sale for under $530 at the time of testing
- Reviewers rated it the best value for most people, though its fan is noisy.
- Source: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C1000+Gen+2)

**Best for extended off-grid trips: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**
- 2,042Wh capacity (1,710Wh measured usable), about 39 lb, under $900 on sale
- Source: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+2000+v2)

**Rugged option: Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**
- 1,536Wh, IP65 rated, shock-resistant, about 40 lb, $1,079 on Amazon at the time of review
- It's quiet and has a comfortable handle, but the port covers are fiddly.
- Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- Buy: [Amazon search for Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+1500+Ultra)

**Mid-size option: BLUETTI AC180**
- 1,152Wh, 1,800W AC, about 35 lb (16 kg), $499 list
- A sale code is listed on a third-party deal site, but I couldn't verify it. Check the price at checkout.
- Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate page; the site earns a commission if you buy through it)
- Buy: [BLUETTI official US store listing via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180), or [Amazon search for BLUETTI AC180](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=BLUETTI+AC180)

## Tips

- **CPAP:** Turn off the humidifier. It can roughly triple the machine's power draw. With it off, a 288Wh unit can run most CPAPs for 3–5 nights.
- **Rough power budget:** A phone charge uses about 10Wh, a camp lantern about 5Wh per night, and a CPAP about 30–60Wh per night.
- **Weight:** Units around 8–10 lb are easy to carry. Units over 25 lb are better kept in a vehicle.
- **Solar:** Most of these pair with portable solar panels. Check whether the panel connector matches the station.
- **Reviews differ:** Testing outlets rank these units differently. OutdoorGearLab rates the Explorer 300 lower than PowerStationGearLab does, so compare the specs that matter most to you.
- **Prices change often.** The prices above come from the review pages and may have changed. Confirm them at checkout.
